title: Walras Retrouvé: Decentralized Trading Mechanisms and the Competitive Price
summary_en: How does the standard competitive-equilibrium price emerge from real, decentralised trading? De Fraja and Sákovics extend the textbook bargaining-foundation result by allowing each trader to interact simultaneously with several traders on the other side of the market — instead of being matched to one. They show that, contrary to the literature's earlier finding, the Walrasian price re-emerges in the limit even with this richer matching structure, providing a cleaner microfoundation for competitive prices.
data_used: Theoretical paper. No data; results from a strategic bargaining model with simultaneous multi-partner matching.
policy_relevance: A foundational paper for thinking about market design in settings where buyers and sellers are not paired one-to-one — e.g., procurement auctions where bidders submit to multiple buyers, online platforms with simultaneous offers, and labour-market matching. Useful background for Hungarian public-procurement reform and electricity-market design (MEKH wholesale auction rules) where decentralised, simultaneous-interaction trading is the norm.
